physicalNotes: No radius or mass of JADES-GS-z14-0 is recorded here: its package frames it at 60,022 pc (object.json worldFrame.bodyRadiusM), half the short side of its picture at its distance, a presentation value.

sources.position: Carniani et al. (2024), Spectroscopic confirmation of two luminous galaxies at z ~ 14, Nature 633, 318 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.18485); Extended Data Table: extended ID JADES-GS-53.08294-27.85563, RA 3:32:19.905, Dec -27:51:20.27 (ICRS)
sources.distance: Comoving distance of the redshift z = 14.1793 (Schouws et al. (2025), Detection of [OIII] 88 µm in JADES-GS-z14-0 at z = 14.1793, ApJ (accepted), arXiv:2409.20549) in the Planck 2018 cosmology: 10347197411.943087 pc, from Astropy 8.0.1 Planck18.comoving_distance (Planck Collaboration 2020, A&A 641, A6, https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.06209). The project's convention for objects placed by redshift (packages/bake/cli/prepare-catalogue-points.mts).
sources.properMotion: Zero: the object is held at its published position; no motion across the sky is applied.
sources.radialVelocity: c z for the redshift z = 14.1793: the redshift written as a velocity, not a motion through space. Schouws et al. (2025), Detection of [OIII] 88 µm in JADES-GS-z14-0 at z = 14.1793, ApJ (accepted), arXiv:2409.20549 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.20549); abstract: z = 14.1793 ± 0.0007 from the [O III] 88 µm line (ALMA).
